clue.text: Ship's described as hollow wreck, so cries loudly

indicators.note: to describe a circle round something is to draw it, so the ship's letters go round the rest

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the usual prefix on a ship's name
qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as

indicators.note: a hollow word keeps only its shell, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A ship surrounded by a gutted wreck, so someone yells about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described as' means drawn around, as one describes a circle, and 'hollow' keeps only the shell of 'wreck'; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To squawk is to shriek harshly, like an alarmed bird, so the verb matches crying loudly.

clue.text: Superior times under second peer

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'under' places the following piece below what comes before it

parts.note: a nob is a slang term for an aristocrat or toff
by is the multiplication word, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Someone superior, multiplied, sits beneath a second lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Being snobby means behaving as if superior to others; a near-synonym of condescending.

clue.text: See 23
Chinese food perhaps later brought up, therefore happy

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up a piece writes it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: 'not now' means at a later time
so means therefore
up means cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: A Chinese meal that, later regurgitated, somehow cheers you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' makes NOT NOW read WON TON. 'Brought up' tempts you towards vomiting, a pun on the food.
explanation.definitionFit: This broth of dumplings is a classic Chinese dish; 'perhaps' flags it as an example.

clue.text: Went with Vicious before Balls

indicators.note: places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: Sid Vicious was the Sex Pistols' bass player
Ed Balls is a British Labour politician, later a TV personality

explanation.surface: A punk musician ahead of a politician, a pairing of two celebrity names.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital letters hide two surnames used as first names: Sid Vicious, a punk musician, and Ed Balls, a former UK cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To side with someone is to support them; past tense matches 'went with'.

clue.text: See 23
Dog crossing river over a snapper

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
the dog's letters go across, round, the river's

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A dog wades across a river above some snapping creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapper' suggests a fish or turtle; it is a simple old camera that snaps photos.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapper is a slang word for a photographer or camera; this is a basic box-shaped one.

clue.text: Bird to catch, tail first

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is moved to the front

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it

explanation.surface: Advice on catching a bird by grabbing its tail first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Revolutionary and you in South African celebration of old

indicators.note: revolution turns things round, so the following words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolutionary figure and you take part in a historic South African festivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a person, but it signals rearranging AND YOU IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Union Day, 31 May, marked the 1910 founding of the Union of South Africa and is no longer a holiday.

clue.text: Attention-seeker voiced song for play

indicators.note: says the word is spoken, giving a different spelling with the same sound

parts.note: hey is a call to get someone's attention
Fever is a well-known song recorded by Peggy Lee

explanation.surface: Someone craving attention sang a number for the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward's 1925 comedy, set at a country house, bears this title.

clue.text: Bulb shining, one lit

parts.note: a lamp that is shining is on
I is the Roman numeral for one
a light that is lit is on

explanation.surface: A light bulb glowing, a single lamp burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a lamp, which the surface plays up; it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen vegetable grows as an underground bulb, botanically speaking.

clue.text: God squeezing armpit, nothing less, showing skill

indicators.note: the god's letters squeeze in, i.e. surround, the next piece

parts.note: a deity is a god

indicators.note: says the following letter is removed from the word before

parts.note: oxter is a Scots and northern English word for armpit
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A god hugging someone under the arm, proving rather deft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing' holds the trimmed armpit word inside the god, and 'less' drops the zero-shaped letter; 'showing' is a link. OXTER is a Scots word, little known outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexterity means manual deftness or adroitness, a synonym of skill.

clue.text: Greeting spoken thus, note, around France and Germany etc? On the contrary

indicators.note: the whole string is turned the opposite way, reading backwards

parts.note: said means spoken
so means thus

indicators.note: the note's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means note well
these are members of the EU, the European Union

explanation.surface: A spoken hello, with a note on European neighbours, and then a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: SAID SO N(EU)B is built, then 'On the contrary' reverses the whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish phrase means good morning, a standard salutation.

clue.text: 14 19 with this actress?

parts.note: the cross-referenced film concerns the Bard's romance; his real wife shares her name with a Hollywood star, so he would be smitten with her

explanation.surface: A question about whom a famous film's hero was besotted with.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright's wife had this name, as does the Oscar-winning star of Les Miserables.

clue.text: Driving restriction implied and set out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, put out of place

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rule for motorists is suggested and laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' looks like a phrase meaning 'laid down', but SET is fodder and 'out' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal maximum on road velocity is a restriction on driving.

clue.text: Brandish weapon, boomerang that is, with adaptation of novel for film

parts.note: to shake a weapon is to brandish it
a spear is a weapon

indicators.note: a boomerang comes back, so the piece is read backwards

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: adapting a work changes it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Waving weapons, returning ones too, accompany a book's screen version.
explanation.walkthrough: IE turned back gives EI, and NOVEL rearranged gives the final four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1998 romantic comedy won the Oscar for Best Picture.

clue.text: Morning type not getting on with loopy character?

indicators.note: says the following letters are dropped from the word before

parts.note: a person can be called a type, as in 'the outdoors type'
taken as written
and means together with

explanation.surface: An early riser, out of favour, joined with a crazy individual.
explanation.walkthrough: PERSON drops ON to give PERS. 'Loopy character' looks like an eccentric person; it is the curly & symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The & sign is written with loops, and a typographic symbol is a character.

clue.text: See 12
A child seizing the day, seeing old fossil

indicators.note: the child's letters grab, enclose, the day

parts.note: a mite is a small child
Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: A youngster seizing the moment, getting a glimpse of an elderly fogey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old fossil' looks like an elderly person; it is an actual fossil. 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammonite is the coiled fossil shell of an extinct marine mollusc.

clue.text: Penultimate from 14 19 serving as a means of defence

parts.note: the second-to-last letter of 14-across is R; read 19 as 'within amour', French for passion, so R goes inside AMOUR
a plate is a serving of food

explanation.surface: The second-last word of a film title, put to work as protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference splits: 'Penultimate from 14' is R, and 19 read as two words puts R inside AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick steel sheathing on warships and tanks protects them, so it is a defence.

clue.text: See 14
Top rule?

definitions.meaning: to top someone is slang for executing them
to rule is to be the head, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off the head kills someone, as 'top' means in slang; split, the word means be in charge.

clue.text: Carrying no bricks? That's criminal!

indicators.note: the hod holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a hod is the open trough a labourer uses for bricks
O, like zero, means nothing or none

explanation.surface: An empty brick trough seems to be an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a labourer turning up without bricks; 'That's' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is short for hoodlum, a gangster or violent criminal.

clue.text: Very poor cryptic clue conceals new editor's initial boozing

parts.note: crap is slang for very poor quality

indicators.note: the scrambled word hides the next letter within itself
something cryptic is obscure, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A terrible crossword clue hides the new editor's drinking habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic clue' looks like the surface's subject, but 'cryptic' signals rearranging CLUE as ULEC, and 'conceals' puts N inside it, giving ULENC before the editor's E.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulence is drunkenness or the sickness after overindulgence in drink.

clue.text: Posh neighbour, utter dope, moving

definitions.note: the nickname of an English football club from Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: the letters are moved around, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An upper-class neighbour proves a complete idiot when on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh' looks like an adjective for the neighbour; it is the nickname of a football club in the English Football League.
explanation.definitionFit: This English football club has long been nicknamed 'the Posh'.

clue.text: Drink some welcome, a daiquiri

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An offer of a drink: some welcome, a daiquiri.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic beverage made by fermenting honey and water.

clue.text: Part that hasn't caught rays, catching a fish

parts.note: skin not exposed to the sun stays pale, white

indicators.note: the part's letters catch, enclose, the next letter

parts.note: a bit is a part

explanation.surface: An untanned body part catching a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rays' tempts a fish reading; they are sun rays.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitebait are tiny young fish such as herring or sprat, eaten whole and fried.

clue.text: Animal sounds like a cow with tail of horse

parts.note: a cow moos, making that sound

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A creature that lows like a cow and has a horse's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a large deer of northern forests, an animal.

clue.text: Gave — or gave in?

definitions.meaning: to yield is to produce or give, as a field gives a crop
to yield is also to surrender or submit

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to produce a return and to submit; past tense fits both definitions.

clue.text: Reconditioned roller surprisingly dearer, agent finally admitted

indicators.note: the rearranged letters let the next letter inside
a surprising change rearranges the letters
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A remoulded tyre is unexpectedly pricier, the agent eventually conceding.
explanation.walkthrough: DEARER rearranged as REREAD takes T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is a tyre whose worn tread has been renewed; tyres roll.
